followUps.verdict: Normal numeric input actions co-invoke separate follow and C2M clears in that order. The preceding input update can return while follow is still active. Static cleanup and event handling do not demonstrate a physical stop.
followUps.method: Read-only exact-build PE exception ranges and Capstone via manager hardened inspect-navigation-static.py and pinned original RiftReader helper; depth 0, no recursive callees, no unwind-chain auto-expansion; manual selected continuations. No REA output or decompilation.

observations.claim: 0x694333 resolves event+0x124 with third argument (event+0x12c == 0); 0x694377 forwards result as action ID and raw event+0x12c byte. 0x69478b is a second dispatch site using zero for the forwarded byte.

After earlier gates reach the switch, action IDs 2-7 converge on the same saved receiver and follow-clear then C2M-clear. Raw event byte zero additionally clears receiver+0x39c for IDs 2/3; both raw-byte branches still reach the clear pair. No branch here makes the pair release-only.

Action update 0x697140 occurs before clears. Its nonzero receiver+0xb60 path sets BL=1 and reaches the return at 0x697634, before downstream mode installation. Other guards include helpers 0x562570 and 0x561be0, whose semantics are not qualified here.

0x697a40(false) queries IDs 2,3,6,7,4,5,8,16 through 0x7b78c0; both input-bit set and clear transitions mark its changed result. Reconciliation calls input update first, then both clears only on a nonzero changed result. This is not an unconditional stop handler.

0x7b20a0 normalizes modifier-like numeric codes then searches a tuple of event code and two modifier fields; match returns entry+0x14, failure returns -1. 0x7b78c0 searches an action-ID tree then tests binding-like records via untraced helpers. No registered human action names or current bindings were recovered.

C2M clear conditionally copies its +0x70/+0x78 handle/owner pair with reference-count-like operations, calls accessor 0x494830 and helper 0x860530, then releases and zeros the component pair and clears activation bit0. With +0x70 zero, it skips helper/owner work but still clears bit0. It does not overwrite vector +0x60/+0x68.

0x860530 searches a tree by the copied handle key. Exact match calls 0x860370(handle,false) before 0x85cae0. Missing key skips both; either path tail-calls 0x4877d0 on the copied pair. 0x860370 dispatches unknown virtual methods over child arrays, zeroes a child +0x11 byte and resets two array ends. Virtual meanings and navigation connection are unknown.

0x562bc0 performs follow-clear then C2M-clear before copying the new coordinate vector and setting activation bit0. Cancellation, replacement and manual-input dispatch therefore share clear routines but remain distinct control paths.

inferences.claim: IDs 2-7 are movement-direction-like actions, supported by input bit reconciliation and downstream mode selection. Exact forward/back/turn/strafe names remain unqualified.
0x860530 and 0x860370 are handle-registration removal/cleanup candidates; the inspected prefix of 0x85cae0 does not prove erase semantics, and cleanup is not established as path-job cancellation.
An input event marked handled at +0x18 and fields cleared cannot alone certify physical stopping, especially because the update helper runs before the clear pair.

rejectedConclusions: IDs 2-7 prove W/A/S/D or named backward/strafe bindings.
The forwarded zero/nonzero event byte is a qualified physical key-up/key-down mapping.
Follow-clear alone clears the separate C2M activation state.
0x860370 virtual calls are proven pathfinding-job cancellation or physical braking.
Input update necessarily installs a new mode before the clears; active follow takes its early return.
A handled event, stopped-follow message, key release or cleared activation bit proves world-space motion stopped.
The native coordinate vector is erased by C2M clear; its writes clear handle/owner and bit, not +0x60/+0x68.
coverageLimits: Exactly 25 unique PE unwind regions in two depth-0 queries, with no queued items. These are regions, not 25 complete source functions.
0x695810 linear decode ends at 0x696921 before 0x6969ec. Used dispatch/return sites and tables precede that end.
0x7b228d linear decode ends at 0x7b2544 before 0x7b255c. 0x7b24fc onward contains switch tables and is not used as executable evidence; the return at 0x7b24f8 precedes them.
0x697c90 has no containing PE exception entry; no guessed leaf boundary or new decoder was used.
0x85cae0 prefix only, plus 0x494830 and 0x697d90 entry regions only: follow-on ranges outside the budget remain unknown.
No global new caller enumeration; qualified callers here are selected PE-aligned local sites plus the preserved prior 16-site report.
No binding UI capture, live memory, process access, debugger, input, executable launch, injection, installation, network operation or import retry.
